key_findings: OSF FLoRA/SCORE reproduction node resolved (SCORE project qpemg); author data (Data by Subject KS.xlsx, 128 rows; 60 US, 68 Indian) and author Stata .do/.log obtained and independently re-run in Python and R.

Preprocessing internally consistent: numactions column equals the per-subject count of button-press rows in the raw DirectRT trial file for all 127 usable participants (1 Indian participant had missing video, excluded).

Focal claim (Study 3 Culture x Condition interaction): paper reports F(1,120)=5.69, p<.02; independently computed F(1,123)=6.12, p=0.0147 (identical across SS types and Python/R). Direction and significance reproduce; exact F and df do not.
Main effects do not reproduce exactly: paper F(1,120)=14.79 (culture) and 11.56 (condition); computed (Type II) F(1,123)=10.18 and 7.42. Both remain significant.

Simple-effect in the construal-of-choice condition: paper t(32)=4.25, d=1.03; within-India choice-vs-control computed t(65)=-4.15, d=-1.014 (t and d close, but reported df=32 does not match actual df=65). Control condition reproduces t<1 (t=-0.87).

Author disclosed in correspondence that his own Stata re-analysis reproduced significance but not the SPSS F-values, speculating on a historical software bug. Reported dfs F(1,120)/t(32) also disagree with the data's actual df (123/65), flagged by SCORE text-tagging.
Overall qualitative conclusion (Americans construe more actions as choices than Indians, driven by the choice condition) is robustly reproduced; exact headline statistics are not.
notes: Matches human FLoRA classification 'computational issues': headline statistics do not reproduce exactly from the author's shared data/code, but the focal interaction is reproduced as significant in the same direction. No paywalled article PDF retained; only data, code, SCORE reports and short OA README kept. Graded CONSISTENT (conclusions hold with disclosed, non-conclusion-overturning deviations), not FULL due to non-reproducing F-values/dfs.
